title: How effective is pre-training of large masked autoencoders for downstream Earth observation tasks?
relevance: Finds that large MAE pretraining helps mainly when the downstream task RESEMBLES the pretraining objective - reconstruction - and that for SEGMENTATION, training from scratch with well-tuned hyperparameters performs comparably or better. This is the direct counterweight to our Search 15 enthusiasm for foundation-model fine-tuning: it does not follow that a pretrained encoder beats our tuned ResNet-101 U-Net on in-domain canopy segmentation. Note the reconciliation, because it is testable: Luo 2025 (ID 107, peer-reviewed) claims the VFM advantage on CROSS-DOMAIN generalization, not in-domain accuracy - so the honest expectation is that pretraining buys robustness across our eras, not a better 2016 IoU.

authors: Romero, J., Lv, Q. & Karimzadeh, M.
title: How do self-supervised remote sensing vision models transfer to downstream tasks?
relevance: Three findings that change how we would run such an experiment: model rankings CHANGE across tasks and adaptation settings so there is no universally best geospatial foundation model; decoder architecture and fine-tuning strategy matter as much as the choice of backbone; and task-relevant information sits in INTERMEDIATE transformer layers rather than final embeddings. That last point is a direct answer to our open question Q15 - if we need a feature space for kernel mean matching or a density-ratio estimate, take intermediate-layer activations, not the final embedding. Also warns that any single-benchmark claim about foundation models should be distrusted, including the ones we cited in Search 15.

title: SatDINO: A deep dive into self-supervised pretraining for remote sensing
relevance: Reports DINO-style contrastive pretraining outperforming the far more common masked-autoencoder approach on remote sensing benchmarks, and - directly useful to us - adds explicit GROUND SAMPLE DISTANCE encoding plus adaptive view sampling as independent components. Our archive spans 7.5-60 cm, an 8x GSD range that our augmentation already bridges but our encoder does not represent; GSD conditioning is a cheaper, more targeted idea than retraining per resolution tier. If we pretrain on our own unlabelled 18-year archive, this says use DINO rather than MAE and condition on GSD.
